# Cheat sheet plus library index: the hybrid prompt, measured
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #140, sha256:9c7280be151100e8a02d3456ab2f9d5c0eac32188f67077e362e97e82a73e8a6). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** data (a pre-registered measurement; hypothesis from the product owner, ranked below the prototype path)
- **Milestone:** Loop tooling: the mob keeps itself running
- **Source:** Product direction, 2026-10-28 (the mob loop always re-tests whether unavailable models are available again) and Decider D88. Found when Copilot's quota ran out mid-run (reset 2026-11-01 00:00 UTC) and its holdout rows were marked unavailable.
- **Depends on:** 134
- **Story:** As the product owner, I want to know whether a compact cheat sheet for the core plus an index of phrase signatures for the library, with full definitions pulled on demand, keeps prompt tokens flat as the library grows at an equal or better pass rate, so that the language can grow past what a cheat sheet can hold.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a Decider written before any row, When it is read, Then it fixes the arms (cheat sheet only, full docs, cheat sheet plus index with on-demand lookup), the library sizes, the tasks, N, the models, the pass bar and the charging rule (every lookup token and every round trip charged, cold no-lookup and lookup-enabled treatments reported separately), and a check fails if it is missing or dated after the first row
  2. Given a library that grows in steps, When each arm is run cold on the same tasks, Then each row records prompt tokens, lookup tokens, round trips, attempts, pass and library size, and the index is built only from the sentence names of phrases (a test shows the index contains no implementation text)
  3. Given the rows, When summarized, Then tokens against library size are shown per arm with no verdict beyond what the Decider pre-registered, beside the codebase-size and growth-study results

## Context

- Pairs with the codebase-size and growth-study cards. On-demand lookup needs tool use or a second turn, which current cold runs disable; the design must allow it in one treatment only. Must not jump ahead of the prototype path. It is a separate question: it does not amend the frozen bar (D32) and does not rescore any stored row.
